new_scholarship.application_method: Separate application, not automatic on admission. Applicants must first be holding a valid University of Tasmania offer; the page states "Students eligible for the Tasmanian International Merit Scholarship will be invited to apply for the Tasmanian Excellence Scholarship after they have received an offer at the University of Tasmania" and "Eligible students will be invited to apply and will receive a link to the scholarship application form." The invitation is issued by the University and carries the link to the scholarship application form. Shortlisted applicants are contacted for an interview after the deadline has closed.
new_scholarship.description: The Tasmanian Aurora Excellence Scholarship is the University of Tasmania's highest academic-merit international scholarship. It provides eligible commencing international students with a 50% reduction in registered tuition fees for the duration of their course, applied as a tuition fee credit after each census date. Bachelor's and honours coursework programs are eligible apart from a named exclusion list, so the award is funded at undergraduate level as well as postgraduate. Selection uses a minimum 90 ATAR or equivalent, an application form, a 300-500 word personal statement and an interview. The benefit is tuition only: the Terms and Conditions state the scholarship does not apply to the Student Services and Amenity Fee, accommodation, insurance, books or other non-tuition costs, and is not redeemable for cash.
new_scholarship.best_fit: High-achieving international applicants with a 90 ATAR or equivalent (or a UTAS degree-level GPA of 6.5/7) who are seeking the largest tuition discount UTAS offers to international students. Because the application is invitation-triggered and runs off the Tasmanian International Merit Scholarship offer route, it suits applicants strong enough on merit to be issued that offer.
new_scholarship.eligibility_summary: Applicants must be classified as an International Student under the University of Tasmania's Application rules, meet the minimum academic requirements (90 ATAR or equivalent; 6.5/7 GPA where the highest qualification is UTAS degree-level study), be enrolled full-time in an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree, not be a student from a Transnational Education (TNE) partner affiliated with the University, not be in receipt of any other University of Tasmania scholarship or any external sponsorship, not be commencing through an articulation agreement with a partner institution, and be commencing the first year of their program from 2027. The Terms and Conditions add that applicants must commence study for the first time, must not have previously commenced a course at the University, must hold a valid offer, must meet admission and English language requirements, and must remain eligible for an Australian student visa where applicable. Named excluded undergraduate programs are the Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine, the Bachelor of Nursing in the Hobart campus, the Bachelor of Applied Science (Nautical Science) and (Marine Engineering), and the Advanced Diploma of Applied Science (Nautical Science) and (Marine Engineering). The scholarship is also not available for fully online programs, foundation studies, non-award study, micro credentials, single unit study, exchange programs, government sponsored students, study through the International Pathway College, or study undertaken at a university location outside Australia unless the University approves in writing.

new_scholarship.selection_notes: Applications are assessed on three published components: meeting the minimum academic requirements for the highest-level qualification (secondary, diploma and degree level of a minimum one-year duration), completion of the application form, and a Personal Statement of 300-500 words. Shortlisted applicants are contacted for an interview after the deadline has closed, so interview performance is the final stage. Applications are assessed for all semester intakes and selection is based on the applicant's highest-level qualification of a minimum of one-year's duration or equivalent. The Terms and Conditions state that scholarships are awarded based on satisfaction of eligibility requirements, published selection criteria which may include academic merit, and available scholarship funding, and that the University may establish scholarship quotas, market-specific allocations or strategic recruitment priorities. All University decisions are final and not subject to review. No published weighting between the assessment components and no published number of awards.
new_scholarship.notes: NAME MISMATCH WITH THE ASSIGNMENT ROW. Row b115 assigned "International Excellence Scholarship - University of Tasmania". The University of Tasmania publishes no award under that name. Its international scholarship portfolio is Tasmanian International Scholarship (25%), Tasmanian International Merit Scholarship (30%), Tasmanian Aurora Excellence Scholarship (50%), Tasmanian Access Scholarship, International Alumni and Family Scholarship, Early Acceptance Scholarship and external scholarships. Note the official page itself refers to it once as "the Tasmanian Excellence Scholarship" in the invitation sentence; that is a variant of the same award, not a separate scheme. DIFFERENT AWARDS ON ONE HOST ARE FINE, TWO RECORDS FOR THE SAME AWARD ARE NOT: this is the only record being produced for utas.edu.au. No absolute AUD figure and no stipend figure is published anywhere on the page, so funding_amount/funding_currency/funding_period are null; the benefit is published only as a 50% tuition-fee reduction, so the amount is expressed as a percentage. programme_detail_official.tuition_coverage_note: The award is a partial tuition waiver, not a full one. The Terms and Conditions state it "provides a tuition fee scholarship equivalent to 50% of the published international tuition fees charged for the enrolled units in each study period for the standard duration of the eligible course, up to a maximum of five years full-time equivalent study", and the page's Value field reads "50% reduction in registered tuition fees for the duration of the course." It covers tuition fees only, at 50%, and the same clause states it "applies only to tuition fees" and "does not apply to Student Services and Amenity Fee (SSAF), accommodation, insurance, books or other non-tuition costs". It also "does not apply beyond the standard published duration of an eligible course", "does not apply to repeated units" and "does not apply to units undertaken in excess of course requirements unless approved in writing by the University". Because half of tuition and every non-tuition cost remain payable by the student, fully_funded is false. No absolute dollar figure is published, so funding_amount and funding_currency are null.

programme_detail_official.description: The Tasmanian Aurora Excellence Scholarship is the University of Tasmania's most selective academic-merit award for commencing international students, providing a 50% reduction in registered tuition fees for the duration of the course, credited to the student's account after each census date. Eligible courses include all undergraduate bachelor and honours coursework programs apart from a named exclusion list, so the award is funded at bachelor's level as well as postgraduate. Applications are invitation-triggered: the University invites applicants who hold an offer and are eligible for the Tasmanian International Merit Scholarship, and sends a link to the scholarship application form. Assessment uses a 90 ATAR or equivalent threshold, the application form, a 300-500 word personal statement and an interview for shortlisted candidates. The benefit is tuition only and is capped at five years full-time equivalent; the Terms and Conditions expressly exclude the Student Services and Amenity Fee, accommodation, insurance, books and other non-tuition costs, and the scholarship is neither redeemable for cash nor transferable.

Reading the 50% as a 50% discount on total cost of study rather than on tuition fees only
Being on an excluded course, or entering through an articulation agreement with a partner institution
Being a TNE partner student, which the University excludes outright
Holding another University of Tasmania scholarship or external sponsorship, which disqualifies the applicant
Missing the intake-specific deadline, because Semester 1 and Semester 2 close on different dates
Not preparing for the interview stage, which shortlisted candidates reach only after the deadline has passed

research_notes.logo: logo_override is null, and logo_probe is an explicit list of nulls rather than an absent key, so a merge stage can tell "verified and deliberately empty" apart from "never checked". WHAT I TRIED: (1) Read the site header markup of every utas.edu.au page fetched - the scholarship page, the international scholarships index and the scholarships index all reference the same header wordmark img with alt "University of Tasmania logo" at https://www.utas.edu.au/__data/assets/git_bridge/0012/1368768/dist/mysource_files/logo.svg. This is the header dark wordmark, so rule 6 (white-on-transparent) would not have been the obstacle. (2) Probed that URL live with curl: HTTP 403, content-type text/html, 5646 bytes, first bytes "<!DOCTYPE html><html lang=\"en-US\"><head><title>Just a moment". (3) Read the footer asset reference in the same markup, https://www.utas.edu.au/__data/assets/file/0020/1415225/utas-footer-logo.svg, and probed it: HTTP 403, text/html, 5583 bytes, same "Just a moment" body. (4) Probed a known-good PNG asset on the same host to test whether the block was specific to SVGs, https://www.utas.edu.au/__data/assets/image/0009/1595250/footer-the-ir1ca.png: HTTP 403, text/html, 5586 bytes, same interstitial. (5) Probed /favicon.ico: HTTP 403, text/html, 5673 bytes, same interstitial. (6) Retried the first three with a full desktop Chrome User-Agent and an image Accept header: still HTTP 403 text/html, 5902/5839/5673 bytes. WHY IT FAILED: www.utas.edu.au sits behind Cloudflare, and the bot-management interstitial is served on direct requests for static assets even when the HTML pages themselves render normally through a full client. Every candidate therefore returned HTML rather than image bytes, which PART D rule 7 excludes outright ("A host whose logo URL returns HTML rather than image bytes is excluded. That is a WAF interstitial or an error page, not a logo"). I did not add the URL on the strength of the markup reference alone, because rule 5 forbids an unprobed URL and rule 4 treats every override as a candidate that still has to pass the image validator. No third-party host, CDN mirror, Wikimedia copy or social asset was substituted, since all of those are hard-banned. logo_host_taken was false for this row, so no existing entry for utas.edu.au is being duplicated or shadowed.

research_notes.degree_level_confirmed: Confirmed directly from the official Terms and Conditions - 2027 on the scholarship page: "Eligible courses include: all undergraduate bachelor and honours coursework programs except excluded programs being: Bachelor of Medical Science and Doctor of Medicine; Bachelor of Nursing in the Hobart campus; Bachelor of Applied Science (Nautical Science); Bachelor of Applied Science (Marine Engineering); Advanced Diploma of Applied Science (Nautical Science); Advanced Diploma of Applied Science (Marine Engineering)". The Eligibility section on the same page separately requires enrolment "full-time in an eligible undergraduate or postgraduate coursework degree", and the academic threshold is published at 90 ATAR or equivalent for secondary, diploma and degree-level study, confirming the award funds a bachelor's degree rather than being postgraduate-only.
